title: Isotropic Min-Norm Risk Formula
statement: For the isotropic linear model (Sigma = I) with i.i.d. features, the asymptotic prediction risk of the min-norm least squares estimator is R(γ) = σ²/(γ(1-γ)) for γ < 1 and R(γ) = r²(1 - 1/γ) + σ²/(γ - 1) for γ > 1, where r² = ||β||² and γ = p/n.
test_plan: Simulate n=1000, p=γn for γ in [0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 1.1, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0]. Generate X ~ N(0, I_p), y = Xβ + ε with β fixed norm r=1, ε ~ N(0, 1). Compute min-norm solution β_hat = X^T(X X^T)^{-1}y. Estimate risk on 10,000 test points. Compare empirical risk to theoretical formula. Pass if relative error < 5% for all γ.
success_criterion: Empirical risk matches theoretical formula within 5% relative error for all tested γ values.

title: Double Descent in Misspecified Model
statement: In the misspecified isotropic model with polynomial approximation bias 1-κ(γ) = (1+γ)^{-a}, the min-norm least squares risk can attain its global minimum in the overparametrized regime (γ > 1) when SNR > 1 and a is sufficiently small (specifically a ≤ 1 + 1/SNR is a sufficient condition).
test_plan: Simulate the misspecified model: y = x^T β + w^T θ + ε. Let x, w be independent N(0, I). Set ||β||² + ||θ||² = r²=5, ||β||²/r² = κ(γ) = 1 - (1+γ)^{-a}. Test a=0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0 with SNR=5. Compute min-norm risk for γ in [0.1, ..., 10.0]. Verify that for a=0.5, the global minimum of the risk curve occurs at γ > 1. Pass if argmin(R(γ)) > 1 for a=0.5.
success_criterion: For a=0.5 and SNR=5, the γ value minimizing the empirical risk is strictly greater than 1.

title: Latent Space Model Monotonicity
statement: In the latent space model where features are generated as x = Zw^T + U with Z ~ N(0, I_d), W fixed, and β aligned with the top eigenvectors of Σ, the min-norm least squares risk is monotonically decreasing in the overparametrized regime (γ > 1) and approaches its global minimum as γ → ∞.
test_plan: Simulate latent space model: d=20, n=200. Generate Z ~ N(0, I_d), W ~ N(0, I_{p,d})/sqrt(d). X = ZW^T + U, U ~ N(0, I). y = Zθ + ξ. Compute min-norm risk for γ in [1.1, 1.5, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0]. Check if risk(γ=1.1) > risk(γ=1.5) > risk(γ=2.0) > risk(γ=5.0) > risk(γ=10.0). Pass if the sequence is strictly decreasing.
success_criterion: The empirical risk values form a strictly decreasing sequence as γ increases from 1.1 to 10.0.

title: Nonlinear Model Universality
statement: For a nonlinear random features model x = φ(Wz) with purely nonlinear activation φ(t) = a(|t|-b), the asymptotic prediction risk of min-norm regression matches the risk of the corresponding linear Gaussian model with the same covariance structure, regardless of the dimension d of the latent space z.
test_plan: Simulate nonlinear model: n=200, d=100. Z ~ N(0, I_d), W ~ N(0, I_{p,d})/sqrt(d). X = φ(ZW^T) with φ(t)=|t|-0.5. y = Xβ + ε. Compute min-norm risk for γ in [0.5, 1.5, 3.0]. Compare to linear model risk with Σ matched to Cov(X). Pass if the difference in risk between nonlinear and linear models is < 0.1 for all γ.
success_criterion: The absolute difference between the empirical risk of the nonlinear model and the theoretical risk of the matched linear model is less than 0.1 for all tested γ.

title: Ridge Dominates Min-Norm
statement: In the isotropic well-specified and misspecified settings, optimally-tuned ridge regression (minimizing risk over λ) achieves a lower prediction risk than min-norm least squares (λ=0) for all values of γ and SNR.
test_plan: Simulate isotropic model (well-specified) and misspecified model. For γ in [0.5, 1.5, 3.0], compute risk for min-norm (λ=0) and for ridge regression with λ optimized via grid search over [1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2, 0.1, 1.0]. Pass if min_λ Risk(λ) < Risk(λ=0) for all γ and both model types.
success_criterion: The minimum risk over the ridge penalty grid is strictly less than the min-norm risk for all tested γ values.

title: Underparametrized Risk Divergence
statement: In the underparametrized regime (γ < 1), the prediction risk of the min-norm least squares estimator diverges to infinity as γ approaches 1 from below.
test_plan: Simulate isotropic model with n=1000. Compute min-norm risk for γ in [0.9, 0.95, 0.99, 0.999]. Verify that the risk increases as γ increases towards 1. Pass if Risk(0.999) > Risk(0.99) > Risk(0.95) > Risk(0.9) and Risk(0.999) > 10 * Risk(0.9).
success_criterion: The risk at γ=0.999 is greater than 10 times the risk at γ=0.9, and the risk is monotonically increasing with γ in the range [0.9, 0.999].
